header.Image: open-dfp-34x-2c on the ODI DFP-34X-2C3, build run21

results.check: The stick runs the kernel of this tree
The boot started the ssh server, omcid and pond
results.evidence: dropbear pid 91 66, omcid pid 83, pond pid 86

results.check: The root is the image's own, read-only from flash or the initramfs of a RAM boot; /tmp, /run and /var are in memory
results.evidence: / the initramfs of a RAM boot; /tmp tmpfs, /run tmpfs, /var tmpfs

results.check: The PTP hardware clock is the ports' timestamping clock, and its pulse comes once a second
results.evidence: ptp0 rtl9602c-ptp, hardware-receive, hardware-raw-clock; 4 pulses 4.000 s apart

results.check: The watchdog runs, and the daemon of the boot feeds it
results.evidence: RTL9602C watchdog, timeout 44 s, active, daemon pid 51

results.check: The host link sfp is up at its speed
results.evidence: sfp up, 2500 Mb/s

results.check: The management address answers on its VLAN of the host link
results.evidence: mgmt: VLAN 4094 on sfp; this run reaches the stick through it

results.check: The packet filter is loaded, dropping by default
results.evidence: 2 chains with policy drop (input, forward), 21 lines

results.check: A port nobody listens on is dropped with the filter and refused without it
results.evidence: filtered: timeout after 3.00 s; unfiltered: refused in 0.001 s; filter restored

results.check: The ssh server offers keys only, no passwords
results.evidence: exit 0:

results.check: The status daemon answers on the host side
results.evidence: HTTP 200 {"ok":true}

results.check: The status page is served on the host side
results.evidence: http/1.1 200 ok, html, with a CSP

results.check: Without the token the daemon's API stays locked
results.evidence: HTTP 401 unauthorised

results.check: With the token the daemon reports the kernel, the ONU and the optics
results.evidence: HTTP 200, kernel: 177 B, onu: 523 B, optics: 94 B

results.check: Downstream is locked: bandwidth maps keep being accepted, none with a CRC error, and no alarm
results.evidence: 7974 bandwidth maps/s, 0 with a CRC error, alarms none

results.check: The ONU is in O5, operation
results.evidence: O5, ONU-ID 1

results.check: The ONU stays in O5 for a minute
results.evidence: 12 reads 5 s apart: all O5

results.check: OMCI messages flow both ways and none is dropped
results.evidence: rx_messages 335, rx_dropped 0, rx_discarded 0, tx_messages 384, tx_errors 0

results.check: omcid answered the OLT's MIB upload
results.evidence: 2 upload(s), last: 207 units over 105 instances (channel 0)

results.check: The GEM ports the OLT created are interfaces, bridged with the host link
results.evidence: 2 GEM interface(s); omcibr0 holds gem257 gem4095 sfp

results.check: Each T-CONT the OLT mapped to an Alloc-ID through OMCI holds that Alloc-ID
results.evidence: T-CONT 0 holds 257, mapped to 257

results.check: omcid raises no alarm on the clean line, with the power level the kernel reports
results.evidence: power level high; no alarm

results.check: Temperature, supply, bias and both optical powers read within the module's warning thresholds
results.evidence: 45.7 °C, 3.22 V, bias 7 mA, TX_power 2.2 dBm, RX_power -27.0 dBm

results.check: A burst from the network side crosses the OLT, the PON and the switch to the host side in hardware
results.evidence: 400000 frames of 1514 B left the bench, 400019 arrived (100.00%) at 420 Mb/s; CPU saw 18; switch: pon took 400000, sfp sent 400019

results.check: A burst from the host side, above the upstream rate, leaves by the PON in hardware and the ONU stays in O5
results.evidence: 400015 frames of 1514 B left the bench, 400000 arrived (100.00%) at 433 Mb/s; CPU saw 19; ONU O5; switch: sfp took 400015, pon sent 400000

results.check: A C-VID translation in the switch rewrites the VLAN of frames both ways across the PON and keeps their priority
results.evidence: 200 frames of VLAN 3001/5 upstream: 200 as 3002/5; 200 of 3002/5 downstream: 200 as 3001/5

results.check: A translation of one priority rewrites the VLAN of that priority's frames alone
The switch pushes a C-tag onto untagged frames upstream and pops it from frames downstream, and pushes an S-tag in front of a C-tag upstream and pops it downstream, with the priorities it is given
results.evidence: 200 untagged frames upstream: 200 as c3003p5; 200 of c3003p5 downstream: 200 as u; 200 of c3001p1 upstream: 200 as s3004p3+c3001p1; 200 of s3004p3+c3001p1 downstream: 200 as c3001p1

results.check: No frame of the management VLAN crosses the PON in either direction, while the frames of another VLAN cross both ways
results.evidence: 200 of VLAN 4094 upstream: nothing, downstream: nothing; 200 of VLAN 3005 upstream: 200 as c3005p0, downstream: 200 as c3005p0

results.check: The stick keeps IPv6 off its PON side and answers neither ARP for its management address nor an IPv6 ping of all nodes from the network side, though the questions reach its CPU; from the subscriber side, in the management VLAN, it answers both
results.evidence: IPv6 on none of pon, cpu, omcibr0, gem257, gem4095; IPv6 addresses on none; arp_ignore 1; 10 ARP requests and IPv6 pings from the network side: 20 reached the CPU, answered 0 ARP, 0 echo, 0 solicitation; from the subscriber side in VLAN 4094: 10 ARP, 10 echo

results.check: ACL rules on the PON port drop frames from the network side or trap them to the CPU, the rule of the lower tc priority deciding whichever was added first, and tc counts the frames for the rule that decided
results.evidence: 200 frames each; no rule: 200 arrived, 0 to the CPU; trap: 0 arrived, 200 to the CPU, 200 counted at 49010; drop: 0 arrived, 0 to the CPU, 200 counted at 49010; trap over drop, added last: 0 arrived, 200 to the CPU, 0 counted at 49020, 200 counted at 49010; drop over trap, added last: 0 arrived, 0 to the CPU, 0 counted at 49020, 200 counted at 49010

results.check: A matchall mirror copies to the host side what the PON port receives and what it sends, both at once, and nothing once it is removed
results.evidence: 2000 frames each way; mirrored, 2000 of those from the network side to this device and 2000 of those from the host side reached the host side; after, 0 and 0

results.check: The switch learns each bench port's address behind the port it reaches it by, and a static address given to the bridge enters its table and leaves it again
results.evidence: host side on sfp: <mac> self; network side on pon: <mac> vlan 4094 self; static: <mac> self static, then gone

results.check: A tbf on the SFP port holds the frames from the network side to its rate in hardware, and its removal gives the full rate back
results.evidence: tbf 200 Mbit/s: 587973 of 1200000 frames arrived at 205 Mb/s, CPU saw 23; removed: 400021 of 400000 at 419 Mb/s, CPU saw 19

results.check: Of several police rules on broadcast the one of the lowest priority value holds the class, through a replace of it too, and a drop of broadcast is an ACL rule that drops
results.evidence: 600 broadcasts at 300/s: 600 passed with no rule, 216 under pref 10 at 100/s, 216 with pref 20 at 1000/s added, 416 with pref 10 replaced at 200/s; dropped by the ACL, 0 passed; 600 after

results.check: A DCB rewrite entry on pon gives the frames of its priority that it sends the PCP of the entry, leaves the PCP of other priorities as it was, and stops with the entry
results.evidence: 100 frames tagged 100 each; under prio-pcp 0:5nd, PCP 0: 100 as 100/5, PCP 3: 100 as 100/3; without it, PCP 0: 100 as 100/0

results.check: A flood to the stick's own address reaches its CPU no faster than cpu_rx_pps says, leaves the CPU at least half its time and the OMCI messages whole, and goes through once the limit is lifted
results.evidence: cpu_rx_pps 5000: of 444160 frames in 10 s the CPU took 50429; a loop of 1.33 s took 1.73 s; OMCI 2 of 2 delivered; lifted: 28360 frames/s

results.check: Multicast snooping: from the network side a group a host joined reaches it and one no host asked for does not, the link-local groups pass, and every report reaches the network
results.evidence: IGMPv2 query 1/1 to the host side; from the network side, unasked 0/200, 224.0.0.251 200/200; join 3/3 to the network, group offloaded, its data 200/200; 3/3 reports again, timer restarted; MLD query 1/1, MLDv2 join 3/3, unasked 0/200, joined 200/200, MLDv1 reports 3/3, timer restarted; leave 1/1, group gone, its data 0/200

results.check: With a static WAN, a LAN host's UDP flow leaves translated to the WAN address and the switch carries it
results.evidence: WAN up in 2 s; 1000 datagrams to start the flow, 28 through the CPU; then 20000 sent and 20000 answered, 8 through the CPU; 21000 of 21000 arrived from 203.0.113.2; 1 flow(s) in the switch

results.check: With a static WAN, a LAN host's TCP connection leaves translated to the WAN address and the switch carries it
results.evidence: 100000000 bytes sent, 100000000 received from 203.0.113.2 at 714 Mb/s; 33 frames through the CPU against some 69060 segments; 1 flow(s) in the switch

results.check: With PPPoE, the stick opens a session with the concentrator, gets an address, and clamps a LAN host's TCP MSS to fit the session
results.evidence: session up in 4 s; ppp0 <address>, MTU 1492; name servers none; SYN MSS 1452, 1452, 1452 through it

results.check: Back in bridge mode, the GEM ports are bridged with the host link again
results.evidence: bridge mode after 0 s; omcibr0 holds gem257 gem4095 sfp after 0 s more

results.check: After the other cases, the kernel log holds no oops, warning, BUG or panic and no switchdev object that a driver failed
results.evidence: 0 of 207 lines

results.check: The host link finds the host's setting as the host moves from 2500BaseX to 1000BaseX with in-band negotiation and back
results.evidence: 1000BaseX with negotiation: back after 3.1 s, sfp 1000 Mb/s; 2500BaseX: back after 1.5 s, sfp 2500 Mb/s

results.check: An armed watchdog that nobody feeds resets the stick within its timeout
results.evidence: timeout 44 s; gone after 55 s, back with a new boot after 653 s
